title: Interpolate kernel latency annotations and add alert-fuzz knobs for noisy SLOs
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: we frequently see noisy SLO alerts that correlate to kernel-level scheduling and small GPU queue stalls that do not map cleanly to per-request token cost or invocation latency. This PR introduces an interpolation layer in the trace enrichment pipeline that attaches estimated kernel latency annotations to invocation spans when direct kernel timing is missing, plus a set of alert-fuzz configuration knobs that reduce alert churn by applying context-aware hysteresis. Changes include: 1) a trace enricher service update that backfills kernel timings using nearest-neighbor interpolation across GPU queue samples and host timestamp anchors; 2) new metrics (telemetry.kernel_latency_interpolated_sum, telemetry.kernel_latency_interpolated_count, telemetry.kernel_backpressure_ratio) and tagging rules to attribute inferred kernel stalls to tenant and model; 3) an alerting config extension (alert-fuzz knobs) that exposes per-alert sensitivity, minimum quiet windows and burst discounts for kernel-driven signals; 4) dashboard: Kernel Latency Atlas (heatmap + timeline) to help SREs triage noisy SLOs; 5) a short runbook describing when to disable fuzz for critical routes and how to tune knobs safely. Implementation notes: the interpolation is conservative (only runs when direct kernel sample missing and adjacent samples are within a 200ms wall window), uses exponential smoothing for noisy samples, and records provenance via trace.annotation(kernel.interpolated=true) so we can audit backfilled values and revert if needed. Checklist: [x] unit tests for interpolation kernel, [x] end-to-end integration test in telemetry-integration, [x] schema migration for new metrics, [x] dashboard + panel + saved query, [x] runbook doc. Related: builds on work in ENG-1989 (trace enrichment refactor). Links: internal runbook RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2034/interpolated-kernel-annotations, deployment playbook link: https://go/redwood/telemetry/deploy-playbook. Note: this intentionally does not change sampling policies; we store an extra boolean flag so any future sampler can opt out of interpolated annotations.

release_notes: Add conservative kernel-latency interpolation to trace enrichment; new kernel latency metrics and a Kernel Latency Atlas dashboard; introduce alert-fuzz knobs to reduce SLO alert churn caused by transient kernel stalls; add runbook with tuning presets.
notes: Because interpolated annotations change telemetry-derived signals, rollout used a dark-launch flag (env TELEMETRY_INTERPOLATION=alpha) for 48h in staging then a canary release across 5% of traffic. No alert drift detected in the canary window. We shipped with conservative defaults and saved override presets for enterprise tenants that opt for stricter SLO enforcement.
